quickStart.item_13: For an immediate threat to life or safety, call Triple Zero (000). From a mobile, 112 may connect to emergency services; use 106 text emergency service if you have a speech or hearing impairment.
quickStart.item_24: For urgent health advice when it is not a life-threatening emergency, call healthdirect on 1800 022 222.
quickStart.item_18: For poison advice, call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26.
quickStart.item_46: Locate and securely extract the ZIP package. Review emergency contacts, health details, legal document locations, insurance, banks, super, and essential liabilities first.
quickStart.item_30: If someone has died, identify the authorised representative and contact each provider using its official bereavement process. Do not access accounts or use credentials without authority.
quickStart.item_39: Keep the export encrypted and do not store passwords, PINs, authentication codes, myGov/myID credentials, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_131: Wills, powers of attorney, guardianship, and advance-care laws and document names vary by Australian state and territory.
legalNotes.item_114: Superannuation may be administered under fund rules and a death-benefit nomination; do not assume super automatically forms part of the estate or follows the will.
legalNotes.item_117: The ATO states Australia has no inheritance tax, but final personal and estate tax returns, capital gains tax, and super tax may still apply. Check current ATO guidance.
legalNotes.item_99: Official: Triple Zero emergency information: https://www.triplezero.gov.au/
legalNotes.item_56: Official: ATO checklist after a death: https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/deceased-estates/checklist-what-to-do-when-someone-dies

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death. Confirm the relevant state or territory process and your authority before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Australia
meta.reviewedBy: Federal sources reviewed; state and territory legal review remains necessary

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Confirm who is authorised to act, secure records, contact relevant providers, and obtain local legal or tax advice where needed.

startHere.0: Follow the state or territory death-registration process and ask which documents are required.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor or other authorised representative.
startHere.2: Contact Services Australia, the ATO, banks, insurers, employers, and super funds through official bereavement processes.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular bills, and claims; confirm responsibility before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of calls, documents supplied, and provider decisions. Never access an account without authority.

legalFramework.0: State and territory probate, succession, powers-of-attorney, and guardianship rules.
legalFramework.1: ATO rules for the final tax return and any deceased-estate tax returns.
legalFramework.2: Super fund governing rules and death-benefit nominations; super may be treated differently from estate assets.
legalFramework.3: Current Services Australia, insurance, creditor, and provider claim requirements.
